({{zh|t=裕隆汽車|p=Yùlóng Qìchē}}) is a Taiwanese automaker and importer.{{cite web|title=Company History|url=http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/history.asp|publisher=Yulon Motor|access-date=2013-09-06|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101124033023/http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/history.asp|archive-date=2010-11-24}} Taiwan's [[List of Taiwanese automakers|biggest automaker]] as of 2010, Yulon is known for building [[Nissan]] models under [[license]].{{cite web|title=Yulon to make Luxgen in China|first = Jason | last = Tan | url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2010/08/03/2003479491|work=Taipei Times|date=2010-08-03}} The original [[romanization]] of the company's name is '''Yue Loong''', but in 1992 the company renewed its logo and switched to the shorter ''Yulon'' name. Historically, it is one of Taiwan's "big four" automakers.{{cite web|title=Leveraging capabilities: models of foreign production in the Taiwanese automotive industry |url=http://web.mit.edu/ipc/publications/pdf/00-013.pdf |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology | first =Teresa M. | last = Lynch |date=December 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091123124439/http://web.mit.edu/ipc/publications/pdf/00-013.pdf |archive-date=November 23, 2009 }} The company has over time evolved as a holding company that encompassed multiple public entities such as Yulon-Nissan Motor, Yulon Financial, Yulon Rental, Carnival Industrial Corporation and others. The group currently has a rivalry with [[Hotai Motor]] Group as the two largest Taiwanese automotive companies. Yulon created a new brand to sell self-designed cars, [[Luxgen]], in 2010. As of 2017 it had a revenue of NT$99 billion (US$3.4 billion) and about 12,680 employees.{{Cite web|url=https://markets.ft.com/data/equities/tearsheet/profile?s=2201:TAI|title=Yulon Motor Co Ltd, 2201:TAI profile - FT.com|website=Financial Times|language=en-us|access-date=2018-01-29}} ==History== Incorporated in September 1953{{Cite book | last = Chen | first = Chia-wen | title = An Economic Analysis of Taiwan's Automobile Industry | publisher = MIT | year = 1995 | page = 16 | location = Cambridge, MA | url = http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120314013952/http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf | archive-date = 2012-03-14 }} as a machinery [[company (law)|company]] by Ching-Ling Yen,{{cite web|title=Chronology|url=http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/chronology.asp|publisher=Yulon Motor|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721155440/http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/chronology.asp|archive-date=2011-07-21}} today Yulon Motor Co., Ltd. is part of the Yulon Group, a Taiwanese [[conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]].{{cite web|title=Affiliated Companies – Automobiles|url=http://www.ylg.com.tw/member_E.php?business=1|publisher=Yulon Group|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101101162442/http://www.ylg.com.tw/member_E.php?business=1|archive-date=2010-11-01}} The company is associated with the creation of a Taiwanese auto industry aided by its government. During 1953–1960 an era of "passive protection" reigned and Yulon grew with the assistance of [[protectionism|protectionary tariff]]s of 40–60%.Chen, Chia-wen, p. 24 Parts and components received substantially lower tariffs to help fledgling carmakers. Early on, Yulon looked for foreign partners, but it wasn't until 1956 that an American company, [[Willys]], agreed to share technology. The next year Yulon began its long-lasting partnership with Nissan.[http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf Chen, Chia-wen] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314013952/http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf |date=March 14, 2012 }}, p. 26 While the first Yulon model was a 1956 jeep, with engine production beginning in September of that year, passenger car assembly only started in 1960 with the [[Nissan Bluebird|Bluebird]] after an agreement with [[Nissan]] was signed in 1957. While primarily building Nissan models and other cars under license, Yulon has designed and produced at least one original family car, the 1986 [[Yue Loong Feeling|Feeling 101]].Chen, Chia-wen, p. 93 (Yulon began producing wholly original products again starting in 2009 with the debut of its [[Luxgen]] brand.) Until July 1994, when they changed to using Nissan badging, the license-built Nissan automobiles had all been branded Yue Loong (Yulon after 1992).{{citation | title = Annual Report 2018 | date = 2019-04-30 | publisher = Yulon Motor Co., Ltd. | page = 4 | url = https://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/upload_img/files/report/2019年度裕隆年報-英文_定版_0613.pdf | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230602145702/https://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/upload_img/files/report/2019%E5%B9%B4%E5%BA%A6%E8%A3%95%E9%9A%86%E5%B9%B4%E5%A0%B1-%E8%8B%B1%E6%96%87_%E5%AE%9A%E7%89%88_0613.pdf | archive-date = 2023-06-02 }}{{cite web | title = Het mysterie Yue Loong |trans-title=The Yue Loong Mystery | language = nl | url = http://www.autoweek.nl/forum/read.php?6,3902757 | work = AutoWeek.nl | publisher = Sanoma Men's Magazines B.V | date = 2009-01-30 }} The Nissan branded [[Nissan Cefiro|Cefiro A32]] entered production in February 1996 and became Taiwan's best selling vehicle.{{cite web | title = Chronology | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110721155440/http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/chronology.asp | url = http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/chronology.asp | work = Company History | publisher = Yulon Motor | archive-date = 2011-07-21 }}{{cite web | title = 'Father of Taiwan's Auto Industry' Dead at 53 | first = Mo | last = Yelin | date = 2018-12-05 | work = Caixin Global | url = https://www.caixinglobal.com/2018-12-05/father-of-taiwans-auto-industry-dead-at-53-101355780.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221226050002/https://www.caixinglobal.com/2018-12-05/father-of-taiwans-auto-industry-dead-at-53-101355780.html | archive-date = 2022-12-26 }} ===Assembler=== With production bases located in China, [[Philippines]] and [[Taiwan]], Yulon makes license-built versions of many automakers' models.{{cite web|url=http://www.luxgen-motor.com/about/|title=About Luxgen – Corporate Story|publisher=Luxgen|access-date=2010-11-13|archive-date=2012-06-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120611034150/http://www.luxgen-motor.com/about/|url-status=dead}} The companies it manufactures in cooperation with include [[Chrysler]], [[Geely]],{{cite web|url=http://english.anhuinews.com/system/2010/10/20/003384735.shtml|title=Chery Shapes Taiwanese Partners as Exporters|date=2010-10-20|publisher=AnhuiNews.com}} [[General Motors|GM]], [[Mercedes-Benz]], [[Mitsubishi]] and [[Nissan]]. It assembles most of the vehicles from [[complete knock down]] kits.{{Citation needed|date=November 2010}} The company has used its design and engineering expertise to localize its manufactures to suit Taiwanese tastes. Yulon began building Nissan automobiles under license in the 1960s. For many years the company worked with the Taiwanese government to develop an indigenous auto industry, aided by special tax reductions for modifying or creating their own designs.{{Cite book | last = Chen | first = Chia-wen | title = An Economic Analysis of Taiwan's Automobile Industry | publisher = MIT | year = 1995 | page = 29 | location = Cambridge, MA | url = http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120314013952/http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf | archive-date = 2012-03-14 }} . Yulon's first attempt in doing so was a car called the [[Yue Loong Feeling|Feeling 101]], based on the Nissan Auster/Stanza of the period. The company followed up with facelifted versions such as the Feeling 102 and the Arex, but the Feeling was discontinued in 1995. Starting in July 1994, Yulon began using Nissan rather than Yulon badging on their products. While Yulon continues to manufacture vehicles for sale on the Taiwanese market, as of 2010 it also imports [[Nissan]],{{Citation needed|date=November 2010}} [[Infiniti]],{{Citation needed|date=November 2010}} and [[Renault]] models for sale in the domestic Taiwanese market. ===Nissan=== Yulon has maintained a strong cooperative relationship with Nissan since 1957. After the 1985 passing of a Taiwanese act, the Automobile Industry Development Act (AIDA), Yulon accepted Nissan taking a 25% stake.Chen, Chia-wen, p. 29 Nissan maintained their ownership in Yulon until at least 2003{{cite web|title=Taiwan: Becoming a Development Base for Toyota, Mitsubishi, Nissan, Ford; Honda Launches Production on Its Own |url=http://www.marklines.com/en/amreport/rep193_200308.jsp |publisher=MarkLines.com |date=2003-08-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100705111130/http://www.marklines.com/en/amreport/rep193_200308.jsp |archive-date=July 5, 2010 }} when a restructuring created Yulon-Nissan Motor Co Ltd, a separate company that focuses on complementing Nissan's mainland China activities with research, design, and manufacturing assistance. [[File:Yulon Arex 3151-T3 20160528.jpg|thumb|the exterior of a face-lift Yulon Arex]] == Corporate Leadership == === Chairmen/Chairwoman === * [[Vivian Shun-wen Wu]] (Madam Wu) (1953–2007) * [[Kenneth Yen]] (2008–2018)https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2018/12/04/2003705450#:~:text=He%20studied%20at%20Rice%20University,including%20textiles%2C%20electronics%20and%20construction. * Yen Chen Li-Yien (2018–present)https://asia.nikkei.com/life-arts/milestone/dream-of-taiwan-car-brand-cut-short-as-yulon-chief-dies === Chief Executive Officers/CEOs === * Kenneth Yen (1990–2018) * Kuo-Hsing Hsu (2018–2024 and 2024–present)https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/company/2201:TT#:~:text=Yao%20Chen%2DHsiang,Shihlin%20Electric%20&%20Engineering%20Corp == Brands == Yulon has marketed cars under three in-house brands: their cars were originally sold as Yue Loong (Yulon from 1992 until 1995), but the company switched to using Nissan badging in 1994. They then went on to create two new in-house brands: Luxgen (released in 2009), and Tobe (released in 2010, ended 2013). ===Luxgen=== {{main|Luxgen}} The first Taiwanese auto brand, Luxgen ({{zh|t=納智捷|link=no}}), was created by Yulon in 2008.{{cite web|title=Taiwan's automobile brand LUXGEN announces its ambition to the world|url=http://www.luxgen-motor.com/news/News-Detail.aspx?_sei_=8F8F2499772D44348E4E6506F50D7B48|publisher=Luxgen|date=2010-03-05|access-date=2010-11-13|archive-date=2011-07-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714003457/http://www.luxgen-motor.com/news/News-Detail.aspx?_sei_=8F8F2499772D44348E4E6506F50D7B48|url-status=dead}} On 18 August 2009, Yulon revealed the first car for its new [[Luxgen]] brand. Luxgen cars are developed under Yulon's R&D center HAITEC,{{cite web|title=Prospect of Chinese sales drives Yulon Motor shares up|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2010/09/07/2003482297|work=Taipei Times|date=2010-09-07}} using engines and transmissions provided by other companies.{{cite web|title=LUXGEN 2.2 L MEFI TURBO ENGINE: Light Weight and Efficient|url=http://www.luxgen-motor.com/news/News-Detail.aspx?_sei_=6AC2D62BF5BB462B9213F3CF99556B05|publisher=Luxgen|date=2010-05-13|access-date=2010-11-21|archive-date=2011-07-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714003923/http://www.luxgen-motor.com/news/News-Detail.aspx?_sei_=6AC2D62BF5BB462B9213F3CF99556B05|url-status=dead}} As of 2010, Luxgen products are sold in Taiwan and [[Oman]].{{cite web|title=Taiwan's LUXGEN MOTOR Signs First International Distribution Agreement|url=http://www.luxgen-motor.com/news/News-Detail.aspx?_sei_=28735BEBE4FD4A129F241C2F036854FF|publisher=Luxgen|date=2010-04-30|access-date=2010-11-13|archive-date=2011-07-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714003540/http://www.luxgen-motor.com/news/News-Detail.aspx?_sei_=28735BEBE4FD4A129F241C2F036854FF|url-status=dead}} ===China Motor Corporation (CMC)=== {{main|China Motor Corporation}} [[File:CMC J Space 006.jpg|thumb|[[CMC J Space]]]] ===Tobe=== [[File:Tobe-M'carEV.jpg|thumb|Tobe M'car EV]] Yulon's second brand, Tobe ({{zh|t=酷比|link=no}}), was established in 2009. From 2010 to 2013, Tobe sold its only model, a re-badged, re-designed [[Geely LC|Geely Panda/LC]] called the [[Tobe M’Car]], in Taiwan and Vietnam.{{cite web|title=Yulon's Tobe car unable to drive in reverse|url=http://www.chinapost.com.tw/business/company-focus/2010/08/07/267796/Yulons-Tobe.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110612200734/http://www.chinapost.com.tw/business/company-focus/2010/08/07/267796/Yulons-Tobe.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 12, 2011|work=China Post|date=2010-08-07}} Plans to enter other [[emerging market]]s exist.{{cite web|title=Yulon introduces new Tobe brand vehicle|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2009/11/18/2003458757|work=Taipei Times|date=2009-11-18}} However, poor sales and the brand image of being a rebadged [[Geely]] led to the end of the brand in 2013. {{clear}} ==Production bases== Yulon has a number of production bases in several countries, including China, [[Pakistan]], [[Philippines]] until 2013, [[Taiwan]] and probably [[Thailand]]. ===China=== Initial production base investment in China for Yulon was buying 5% ownership in a Southern China production base in the 1990s. 2000 saw another, larger Chinese production base investment this time of 25%. The latter acquisition was probably in Fengsheng Motors, a [[Dongfeng Motors]] subsidiary. As of 2003, Yulon had 25% ownership in the subsidiary yielding access to production bases in [[Huadu District]], [[Guangzhou]], Guangdong and [[Xiangfan]], Hubei. ===Philippines=== In 1999 Yulon bought a 75% ownership of Nissan's newly built production base in [[Santa Rosa, Laguna|Santa Rosa]], [[Laguna (province)|Laguna]] state.[https://web.archive.org/web/20170317121759/http://dirp3.pids.gov.ph/ris/dps/pidsdps0042.pdf Increasing Globalization and AFTA in 2003: What are the Prospects for the Philippine Automotive Industry?]. Rafaelita A.M. Aldaba. Philippine Institute for Development Studies. Page 35, "Nissan: Worriedly Awaiting the Signal from Japan". This occurred after the Nissan Motor Company pulled out of the Philippines after the Asian market crises caused poor sales in the country. In 2013, it was announced that Nissan Motor Company of Japan will be again taking over Nissan in the Philippines.{{cite web|url=http://www.topgear.com.ph/news/industry-news/nissan-motor-co-to-return-to-ph-this-year-by-merging-nmpi-and-umc|title=Nissan Motor Co. to return to PH this year by merging NMPI and UMC|website=topgear.com.ph|access-date=4 December 2018}} This comes after dismal sales and poor model updates from Yulon Taiwan, which ranked Nissan Philippines well below local rivals from Toyota, Mitsubishi, and Hyundai—not reflective of its ranking as no. 6 global carmaker.{{cite web|url=http://oica.net/wp-content/uploads/ranking.pdf|access-date=2023-08-27|title=WORLD RANKING OF CAR MANUFACTURERS - Year 2011|archive-date=2015-03-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150319082135/http://oica.net/wp-content/uploads/ranking.pdf|url-status=dead}} == Joint ventures == All of Yulon's joint ventures in mainland China are with [[Dongfeng Motor]].{{citation needed|date=May 2015}} ===Dongfeng Yulon=== {{main|Dongfeng Yulon}} A joint venture with Chinese automaker [[Dongfeng Motor|Dongfeng]], called Dongfeng Yulon (or Dongfeng Luxgen{{cite web|title=Dongfeng-Luxgen formally announce JV partnership|url=http://www.chinacartimes.com/2010/12/14/dongfeng-luxgen-formally-announce-jv-partnership/|work=China Car Times|date=2010-12-14}}), was set up in 2009 and will manufacture Yulon's [[Luxgen]] models in China after the completion of a planned production base in [[Hangzhou]] in 2011. The cars will be sold in China. On July 8, 2019, Luxgen signed MoU with Mongolian company AGT Auto to build its first car assembly factory in Mongolia.{{cite web|title=Yulon's LuxGen heading to China|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2010/02/17/2003466063|work=Taipei Times|date=2010-02-17}} Dongfeng Yulon entered bankruptcy in 2020. ===Fengshen Automobile=== In 2003, Yulon had part ownership in a subsidiary of [[Dongfeng Motor]], Fengshen Automobile Co Ltd. ==See also== * [[List of companies of Taiwan]] * [[List of Taiwanese automakers]] * [[List of Nissan vehicles Yulon Motors has built under license]] * [[List of motor scooter manufacturers and brands]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} == External links == {{commons category|Yulon Motor}} * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070103122612/http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/index_en.asp Yulon Motor] – English official site {{Automotive industry in Taiwan}} [[Category:1953 establishments in Taiwan]] [[Category:Car manufacturers of Taiwan]] [[Category:Vehicle manufacturing companies established in 1953]]
extract:
Yulon Motor Co., Ltd. (Chinese: 裕隆汽車; pinyin: Yùlóng Qìchē) is a Taiwanese automaker and importer. Taiwan's biggest automaker as of 2010, Yulon is known for building Nissan models under license. The original romanization of the company's name is Yue Loong, but in 1992 the company renewed its logo and switched to the shorter Yulon name. Historically, it is one of Taiwan's "big four" automakers. The company has over time evolved as a holding company that encompassed multiple public entities such as Yulon-Nissan Motor, Yulon Financial, Yulon Rental, Carnival Industrial Corporation and others. The group currently has a rivalry with Hotai Motor Group as the two largest Taiwanese automotive companies.
Yulon created a new brand to sell self-designed cars, Luxgen, in 2010.
As of 2017 it had a revenue of NT$99 billion (US$3.4 billion) and about 12,680 employees.
